text: Cassava hay (about 25% protein) can be produced on-farm: plant cassava on ridges spaced 40 cm between stems and 60 cm between rows; the first harvest comes at about 3–4 months of growth, with subsequent harvests every 2 months from re-growth, giving at least 4–5 harvests per year; after harvesting, dry the leaves for 1–2 days to make hay. Cassava naturally contains a toxic compound (cyanide/HCN); drying reduces HCN levels by more than 90%, making the leaves safe to feed. Sun-drying reduces moisture from about 90% to 15%, and dried cassava hay can be stored for many weeks.
